statement: Assume the hypotheses and conclusions of Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2 for a scalar height. We retain their notation and record the conditions used below. Let µj converge on compact tests to ν = qHn|L, where q > 0 and L is an n-plane through 0. Here Hn|L has Euclidean normalization, equal to Lebesgue measure in orthonormal coordinates on L. Let uj satisfy (5.5) with |ej| ≤ 1, let wj = uj/δj, and let v be the common limit given by Lemma 4.2. Suppose δj > 0, δj → 0, Kj → ∞, and, for some fixed 0 < γ < 1 and M < ∞, Z B(0,2k) |uj|2 dµj ≤ Mδ2 j 2k(n+2+2γ) (0 ≤ k ≤ Kj), δ−1 j 2−Kj −→ 0. (5.7) Assume that there are radii Aj → ∞ such that, for every j and every compact Lipschitz test ξ supported in B(0, Aj) with R ξ dµj = 0, |Rµj (ξ)| ≤ C(Lip ξ + 1)δ3 j . (5.8) The constant here is independent of j and of the test. Then v has finite local fractional energy and satisfies Z L |v(x)|(1 + |x|)−n−2 dHn (x) < ∞. (5.9) After identifying L isometrically with Rn, for every compactly supported smooth complex function g with R Rn g = 0, Z Rn v(x)Lg(x) dx = 0, Lg(x) = 1 2 Z Rn 2g(x) − g(x + h) − g(x − h) |h|n+1 dh. (5.10) The integral on the left is absolutely convergent. The same conclusions hold simultaneously for the finite family of normal heights in Lemma 4.2, without further extraction.
